issue: Can a federal court modify a sentence that the President has already commuted, such that a § 3582(c)(1)(A) motion to reduce that sentence is not moot?

sides.position: A court cannot disturb a presidentially commuted sentence, even by further reducing it.
An executive commutation only modifies the execution of the judgment, so a court can still correct its own errors in the original sentence and may sometimes reduce a commuted sentence.

quote: A circuit split exists on whether a court can modify a commuted sentence.
cite: United States v. Jonathan Wright, No. 24-2057 (8th Cir. 2025)
